items.title: Joe Watkins Interview, 1961-01-20
items.q: I, wherever Baby Dodds was playing I was always there. And actually I got a lot from, learned a lot from him.

ctx.x: And, well, he got his inspiration from Bunk. And I got my inspiration from Henry Martin, Black Benny, Red Happy, Baby Dodds. But Baby Dodds used to play in the Orleans during them times. Yeah. Well, after I got old enough I used to go to dances. I, wherever Baby Dodds was playing I was always there. And actually I got a lot from, learned a lot from him. Oh, sure. Yeah. Well, when I, around 1918, I was taking press roll lessons from Henry Martin. Yeah. He was a left-hander like me.

items.title: Joe Watkins Interview, 1960-03-16
items.q: Well I used to watch Baby Dots do that you know and that's where I learned that from him

ctx.x: Well I used to watch Baby Dots do that you know and that's where I learned that from him because I used to watch him when he used to play up on the old Temple roof garden.

items.title: Joe Watkins Interview, 1969-03-24
items.q: well I used to go listen to most of the Baber Dodds.

ctx.x: Okay, well we're interviewing Joe Watkins this March 24th, 1969. Just going from what you're about to say, Joe, about when you started music.

When I started, I started in 1920s. Well that was quite a few years after George Lewis and Paul Barbrain. Well I always did love drums because I was born in the third ward and that was, a section for jazz probably because Lee Armstrong was from that ward. He was born and raised around there. And I don't know about Joe Oliver because I always heard that Joe was not exactly from the Orlins. But it was him, Lee Armstrong, Funk Johnson, and you had Manuel Moneta. And, uh, was this other fella's name, uh, was a good…
What sort of date was this? Huh? What date was this about?
